title: Cast Away
tagline: At the edge of the world, his journey begins.
about: A FedEx troubleshooter survives a crash in the Pacific and spends four years alone on an island with a volleyball called Wilson.
cue: Serve the crab when Chuck finally gets his fire going.
faces: “You wouldn't have a match by any chance, would you?”

    Off the reefChargrilled crab claws with garlic butterGotta love crab. Blistered on the coals with lime.How to make it1kg cooked crab claws, cracked80g butter, softened3 garlic cloves, crushed1 red chilli, finely chopped1/2 cup coriander, chopped2 limesMash the butter with the garlic, chilli, coriander and the zest of one lime.Grill the claws over hot coals or a barbecue, turning, until smoky and hot through.Toss with the garlic butter until it melts, then serve with lime wedges.Cracked coconut and lime cevicheChuck works out how to open coconuts. Kingfish cured in lime and coconut milk.How to make it400g sashimi-grade kingfish, diced4 limes, juiced125ml coconut milk1 red chilli, finely chopped1/2 red onion, finely diced1 Lebanese cucumber, diced1/2 cup coriander leaves1 bag plain corn chipsToss the fish with the lime juice and a good pinch of salt and chill for 10 minutes.Drain off half the lime juice and stir in the coconut milk, chilli, onion and cucumber.Scatter with coriander and serve in coconut shells or bowls with corn chips.Fresh coconut milk on the sideA natural laxative, says Chuck.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Island mainsSpearfished whole snapper over the coalsChuck learns to spear fish. Whole snapper stuffed with lemon and herbs.How to make it2 whole snappers, about 800g each, cleaned and scaled3 tbsp olive oil2 lemons, sliced1 bunch dill4 garlic cloves, sliced2 banana leaves of or sheets of foil1 limeScore each fish three times on both sides, rub with oil and salt, and stuff with lemon, dill and garlic.Wrap loosely in banana leaf or foil.Cook over medium coals or a hot barbecue, turning once, until the flesh flakes at the bone.Unwrap, squeeze over lime and serve straight from the leaf.Memphis dry-rub pork ribsChuck keeps the watch on Memphis time. Slow pork ribs with a paprika crust.How to make it2kg American-style pork ribs2 tbsp smoked paprika2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp garlic powder1 tbsp onion powder1 tsp cayenne pepper1 tsp dried thyme125ml apple cider vinegarMix the paprika, sugar, garlic and onion powders, cayenne, thyme and 2 tsp salt, and rub all over the ribs.Wrap tightly in foil and bake at 150°C until tender.Unwrap, mop with the vinegar, dust with a little more rub and finish over hot coals or under the grill until crusty.Cut between the bones and serve.Campfire TreatsAngel wings pavlova with mango and passionfruitThe one package Chuck never opens. Crisp meringue piled with cream and mango.How to make it4 egg whites220g caster sugar2 tsp cornflour1 tsp white vinegar300ml thickened cream2 mangoes, sliced4 passionfruitsWhisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time until thick and glossy.Fold in the cornflour and vinegar and shape into a round on a lined tray.Bake at 120°C for 75 minutes, then cool in the oven with the door ajar.Whip the cream, pile it on and top with mango and passionfruit pulp.To drinkDr Pepper over two cups of iceOne Dr. Pepper and two cups of ice. Chuck likes ice now.How to make it4 x 355ml cans of Dr Pepper2 bags of ice1 lime, cut in wedgesFill 8 cups with ice, two for each person.Pour the Dr Pepper over and add a lime wedge.A 1992 full-bodied grape juiceJust grape juice, says Stan. Not for the pilot.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
